subject: Private connectivity ops screener + CIDR / allowlist asks
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@quantsolve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private connectivity ops screener + CIDR / allowlist asks

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side so NetOps has a clean handoff.

Summary from call:
- QuantSolve confirmed preference for a private deployment (Private VPC) for regulated workloads (PII datasets).
- Primary concerns: egress lock-down, tenant isolation, and auditability for inbound model telemetry.
- You were evaluating PrivateLink vs VPC Peering — NetOps wanted to see CIDR blocks, proposed ports, and whether the RDW control plane will be egressed via the customer's NAT or via our managed endpoints.

What we need to unblock qualification (action items):
1) Provide a short CIDR list (or VPC range) from your side for allowlist testing. If you have multiple envs (staging/prod) indicate both.
2) Confirm whether you can accept PrivateLink endpoints (interface endpoints) in your account, or if peering is the only approved path.
3) Confirm who will host NAT/Gateway for egress to our control-plane IPs (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
4) Any proxy/firewall rules that will do deep TLS inspection or mTLS requirements (if yes, flag so we can include a mutual-auth path).

Attached is our private deployment preflight checklist (short) for NetOps to review. If you can send the CIDR file (or a slide) that lists the VPC ranges and point-of-contact, we’ll validate the flow and then schedule a NetOps handoff meeting next week.

Proposed next meeting: NetOps deep-dive Wednesday 9/22 11:00am PT — does that work for your team?

Thanks,
Aditya
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

---
"On Mon, Sep 19, 2027 at 13:20 Olivia Park <olivia@quantsolve.com> wrote:
> From: Olivia Park <olivia@quantsolve.com>
> To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
> Cc: Quantsolve NetOps <netops@quantsolve.com>
> Date: Mon, 19 Sep 2027 13:20:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Private connectivity ops screener + CIDR / allowlist asks\>
>
> Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap.
>
> Quick answers: we prefer peering for now (security policy) but NetOps will reconfirm whether interface endpoints are acceptable for non-prod. I attached our working CIDR list (qsolve-cidr-list.txt) and a short network contact sheet.
>
> On the NAT question: our Security team wants the customer to manage egress (NAT gateway in our account) and we won’t permit Redwood to route egress through a 3rd-party-managed NAT.
>
> For TLS: we do not perform TLS interception, but we do require downstream servers to present a cert validated by our internal CA for mTLS in prod workloads.
>
> 9/22 11:00am PT should work — looping in NetOps to confirm.
>
> —Olivia
> Head of CloudOps, QuantSolve
>

> Quick note: if QuantSolve requires mTLS for data-plane or control-plane connections we'll need to validate cert chaining and possibly add a mutual-auth option on our egress endpoints. I'll add our infra checklist item to the attached preflight PDF and flag the engineering-hours estimate for the team (small config work + cert exchange).
>
> Also want to confirm whether QuantSolve's prod VPC uses a public egress IP set (static) or if egress is via elastic NATs that could change — that affects our allowlist process.
>
> Ben
> Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
>

"On Tue, Sep 21, 2027 at 09:02 Quantsolve NetOps <netops@quantsolve.com> wrote:
> From: Quantsolve NetOps <netops@quantsolve.com>

> Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Private connectivity ops screener + CIDR / allowlist asks\>
>
> Hi all — looping in our network engineer Chris (chris@quantsolve.com). Here are the specifics from our side: 
> - Prod VPC CIDR: 10.20.0.0/16
> - Staging VPC CIDR: 10.21.0.0/16
> - We use a set of 3 static egress NAT IPs for prod (10.20.0.250/32, 10.20.0.251/32, 10.20.0.252/32) — these are public-mapped via our provider.
> - Firewall allows outbound 443 and 53 to our managed DNS only; we allow 443 inbound from our peered VPN ranges.
> - We do not support interface endpoints in prod; staging is negotiable.
>
> Please confirm the control-plane egress IPs you expect Redwood to present so we can add to the allowlist.
>
> Attaching a short NetOps intake form (filled) and the CIDR list you requested.
>
> Regards,
> Quantsolve NetOps

> 3) I'll send a short note on the mTLS cert exchange process and requirements for prod environments so the security team can review ahead of the meeting.

> For tracking: I uploaded the signed intake form and the filled CIDR list to the HubSpot deal (link below) and attached the preflight checklist with our notes. If anyone prefers, I can also start a Confluence page for the deployment runbook.
